paragraphs.source_en: Generally speaking, whenever some incident occurs, it is because the blood has rushed to the head. “A rush to the head,” as the words themselves indicate, means that something rises upward in reverse. On this point, neither Gehlen, nor Paracelsus, nor even the old-fashioned Bian Que would raise any objection. The only question is where it rises to, and in what manner it rises. And what exactly it is that rises is also a matter for debate. According to the ancient traditions of Europe, four kinds of fluids were said to circulate within the human body. The first is the thing called choler; when this fluid rises, one grows angry. The second is called phlegm; when this fluid rises, the nerves become dull. The third is melancholy, which makes a person gloomy. The last is blood, which gives strength to the limbs. Later, as civilization advanced, phlegm, choler, and melancholy somehow disappeared, and today only blood is still circulating as it did in olden times. Therefore, if anyone suffers a rush to the head, I think it can only be his blood that is at work. Moreover, the quantity of blood in each person is fixed; though it varies somewhat according to temperament, in general each person possesses about five sho and five go. Consequently, when these five sho and five go rise upward, only the part they reach becomes fiercely active, while the other parts, feeling the lack of blood, turn cold. It is just like the time of a police-box burning, when all the policemen gather at the police station and not a single one remains in the streets. Diagnosed medically, that too is what one might call a rush to the head on the part of the police. To cure this rush to the head, the blood must be redistributed evenly through all parts of the body as before. To do that, one must bring down the stuff that has rushed upward. There are various ways to accomplish this. My master’s late father, I am told, used in such cases to place a wet hand towel on his head and warm his legs in the kotatsu. As the Treatise on Cold Damage says, “A cool head and warm feet are signs of long life and freedom from calamity.” Thus the wet hand towel is something that must not be omitted for even a single day in the art of longevity. If that will not do, one may try the method commonly employed by monks. It is said that mendicant monks, wandering priests with no fixed abode, always take trees below and stones above as their lodging. This “trees below and stones above” is not for the sake of ascetic hardship; it is entirely a secret method for lowering a rush to the head, devised by the Sixth Patriarch while he was pounding rice. Try sitting on a stone yourself; naturally your backside will grow cold, and when the backside grows cold, the rush to the head subsides. This is the natural order of things, and there is not the least room for doubt. In this way, many devices have been invented for lowering a rush to the head, but it is regrettable that no good method has yet been devised for inducing one. Taken in a general way, a rush to the head seems a phenomenon that does harm and no good, but there are cases in which one must not judge so hastily.

paragraphs.source_zh: 一般说来，某一事件所以发生，都是由于虚火上升的缘故。“虚火上升”正如字面所示，是火在上升。关于这点，格林也好，帕森斯也好，就连老顽固的扁鹊，都不会提出异议。只不过上升到什么程度，又是如何上升的，却是个问题。而且，到底是什么在上升，也是个争论的问题。根据古代欧洲人的传说，据说在人的体内有四种体液在循环运行。第一，是所谓“怒液”，这种体液一旦上升，就会发怒。第二，叫做“钝液”，这种液体一旦上升，神经就会变得迟钝。第三是“忧液”，它会使人忧郁。最后是“血液”，这就使人四肢健壮。以后，随着人文的发展，怒液、钝液、忧液不知什么时候没有了，到了现在，只剩下血液还和过去一样在循环运行。所以，如果有谁虚火上升，我觉得肯定是他的血液在作怪。而且每一个人的血液的分量都是固定的，虽然根据性格的不同，每个人多少有些增减，但是大体上每一个人都保有五升五合那么多。因此，这五升五合的血液一旦上升，那么，上升所到的部位，就活跃得十分厉害，而其他部位则会因血液缺乏而发冷。这正如同群众烧警察岗楼时，警察全都集中在警察署里，大街上连一名警察也不见踪迹一样。如果从医学诊断的角度来说，有人就说它是警察的虚火上升。那么，为了医治好这种虚火上升，必须像从前一样把血液重新分配到体内的各部位。为了做到这点，就应该将上升的虚火降下来。这有种种方法。我家主人已故的老太爷遇到这种情况，据说是用一块湿手巾顶在头上，然后将两腿伸进“被炉”里去取暖。正像《伤寒论》中指出的“头寒足热乃延命息灾之征也”。这种用湿手巾顶在头上，对于长寿法来说，是一日不可缺的哩。如果不用此法，也可试一试和尚们经常用的方法。那些居无定所的沙门、游方行脚的和尚，据说他们总是在树下石上歇宿的。所谓“树下石上”，并不是为了实现他们的难行苦行，完全是为了医治虚火上升，禅宗第六祖在舂米当中想出了这个秘法。各位也可以自己试试，坐在石头上自然会感觉屁股发凉，屁股一凉，虚火就会下降。这是自然的顺序，也是无可怀疑的。这样，虽然发明了种种方法使虚火下降，但遗憾的是，还没有发明出能惹起虚火上升的良方。一般人的想法，认为虚火上升对人体是有害无益的，但也有另外的情况。
